newsitem.title: GERMANY: Spiegel magazine tops German magazine sales poll.
newsitem.headline: Spiegel magazine tops German magazine sales poll.

text.p: German weekly news magazine Der Spiegel topped the turnover tables of German periodicals in 1996 after gross sales grew 10 million marks to 671 million marks, Spiegel said in a statement on Monday.

The 1.4 percent hike in advertising and sales at the weekly magazine put Spiegel just ahead of 1995's winner, Stern magazine, Spiegel said in a statement, quoting research by the media industry newsletter, kress report.
Turnover at Stern contracted 16 million marks, or 2.4 percent, to 664 million marks. In third place was the Munich-based magazine Focus, which saw a 3.8 percent sales hike to 512 million marks.
Spiegel saw a slight fall in sales, which it made up for in increased advertising revenue, the statement said, while Stern saw both sales and advertising revenue fall.
Focus saw increases in both sales and advertising which helped it knock the Sunday newspaper Bild am Sonntag out of third place.
Der Spiegel, which translates as "the mirror", celebrates its 50th birthday this year.
